title: Mid-course synthesis: a hypothetical causal loop in two frames
promptMarkdown: Alice and Bob meet at $(t,x)=(0,0)$; Bob moves at $v=0.9c$. At $t_0>0$, Alice sends a hypothetical controllable signal at $u=2c$ in her frame. Bob replies immediately at speed $-2c$ in his frame. Derive the outgoing reception event B and Alice's reply-reception event C. Show that C precedes Alice's original emission while the reply goes forward in Bob's coordinate time. Provide event tables and labelled diagrams in both frames; classify both signal legs; identify every assumption about the hypothetical device. Explain why this does not prove that spacelike correlations alone cause contradictions.
hintLadder: Intersect the outgoing signal line with Bob's worldline.
Apply the Lorentz equations to the displacement from B to C, not merely a velocity formula with an ambiguous time sign.
Compute $\Delta t\prime$ directly to verify Bob's emission order.
List what permits Bob to send a new message, rather than just observe a correlation.

criteria.criterion: Both event tables and transformed signal legs are derived consistently.
